text:
taylor_support: Heads-up — ACME reported objects still visible after they changed default retention to 30d and issued deletes yesterday. They see 202 from DELETE but items still returned by list API. Need triage.

alex_engineer: Can you paste one example object id + the exact DELETE request/response?

maria_sre: Also include the object's metadata dump (/objects/{id}/metadata) and the tenant retention config if you have it. Could be a customer-managed retention vs platform default mismatch. :thinking_face:

 taylor_support: Object id: obj-acme-9382. Customer DELETE payload was: 
```
DELETE /v1/objects/obj-acme-9382 HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```
Response we logged: 
```json
{"status":"accepted","delete_id":"del-9382","queued_at":1765340000,"note":"will respect retention policy"}
```
Metadata snapshot: 
```json
{"id":"obj-acme-9382","tenant":"acme-llc","retention":{"type":"customer_managed","expires_at":1768000000,"hold":false}}
```
They said they changed account default retention from 90d->30d on 1765200000.

amal_security: OK. Two quick thoughts: 1) If retention.type == customer_managed then deletes will be deferred until that retention expires or the tenant clears it. 2) We should check if there is any active legal/retain flag set at a different subsystem (billing/exports).

alex_engineer: I ran a quick check against the deletion queue consumer logs for delete_id del-9382: 
```
[1765340100] enqueued del-9382 tenant=acme-llc
[1765340500] worker-3 attempted delete -> retention check failed: customer_managed (expires 1768000000)
```
So system honored the customer_managed retention. That matches metadata.

maria_sre: Do we have any audit-log entries for their API call? They claim we acknowledged but object still visible. If audit logs show the DELETE and the retention decision we can explain timeline to customer.

infra_bot: Audit query: search(audit.table, tenant="acme-llc", op="DELETE", object_id="obj-acme-9382", since=1765330000, until=1765350000) -> 1 entry found. Decision: retention=customer_managed, action=defer.

 taylor_support: Customer is pushing back — they say "we didn't set customer_managed retention for these objects" and pointed to their UI which shows default retention 30d. They suspect stale objects from before the change should have been eligible for immediate purge.

amal_security: Two possibilities: 1) These objects were created under a previous policy that set explicit per-object customer_managed retention. Changing account default doesn't retroactively override per-object retention. 2) There may be a migration/backfill that created explicit retention tags on older objects. We need to check object creation timestamps and retention tag source.

alex_engineer: Agreed. I pulled the object timeline: 
```
created_at: 1761000000  # older than default change
retention_assigned_at: 1761100000
retention_source: api (put with retention=true)
```
So this object has an explicit per-object tag. Default change won't clear it.

maria_sre: Also verify there are no KMS/HSM holds preventing physical purge. Run key access logs for their CMK.

alex_engineer: Quick KMS check: key acme-cmk last-used 1765400000, no denied decrypts in window. No HSM 'lock' flags.

 taylor_support: Customer is asking for an accelerated purge. What are options?

amal_security: We can: 1) Advise customer to clear per-object retention via their management API (requires tenant admin). 2) If they request us to force purge, we need signed authorization and an approval from legal because it's a customer_managed retention change. 3) If there's a legal hold on export or litigation, we cannot purge — need legal confirmation.

alex_engineer: For the customer-managed path, sample admin API to clear retention: 
```bash
POST /v1/tenants/acme-llc/objects/obj-acme-9382/clear_retention
Body: {"reason":"customer_request_admin_clear","signed_by":"tenant_admin@acme"}
```
After that the deletion worker will resume and object should be removed within the normal deletion window.

maria_sre: I'll also check whether any caching layer (CDN/prefix cache) is serving stale GET results. If object truly deleted but still returned by list, that's a different bug. Please confirm list API shows full metadata (retention fields) vs cached index.

 taylor_support: Confirmed list API shows retention metadata still present (so not just CDN). Customer says they don't have admin-level token to run clear_retention. They provided a signed request from their security contact but we need to validate and escalate.

amal_security: Ok I'll spin up an internal escalation. We need: (1) tenant admin confirmation email, (2) written request to Redwood Security to perform admin clear, (3) legal sign-off if they assert any compliance constraints.

alex_engineer: Action items: I will add a note to deletion consumer to surface retention_source and assigned_by in logs for easier future triage. maria_sre will verify no indexing/caching issue. amal_security will handle escalation path and validate signed request. taylor_support will coordinate with customer and collect tenant admin confirmation.

infra_bot: New escalation ticket created: INC-2026-0456. Owners: amal_security, alex_engineer. SLA target: 24h initial response, 72h resolution depending on legal input.

 taylor_support: Thanks everyone — looping in customer with interim message: "We see these objects have explicit per-object retention assigned before your default change. To proceed with immediate purge we need your tenant admin to submit a signed admin-clear request or request Redwood to perform the clear with legal approval. We've opened INC-2026-0456 and will update within 24h." :thumbsup:

amal_security: I'll reach out to Legal for expedited review if ACME requests Redwood-initiated clear.

maria_sre: If ACME supplies tenant-admin request we can usually clear + remove within 2 hours (assuming no legal hold).

alex_engineer: Documenting repro steps for support runbook: 
1) get object id, delete_id, and tenant admin confirmation
2) query /objects/{id}/metadata -> check retention.type and retention_source
3) audit logs for delete_id -> confirm defer decision
4) if customer_admin_clear provided -> call clear_retention endpoint -> trigger deletion worker
5) verify deletion via list API and audit entry for physical removal

 taylor_support: Closing the loop with ACME now. Will post updates to INC-2026-0456. :eyes:
